turns.doctor_question: Hello, please have a seat. What brings you in to see me today?
turns.patient_response:
Well, I'm here because... honestly, for months now I’ve been seeing the exact same pattern, and it's getting ridiculous. My sister’s appointments keep getting moved around, her bills show up completely wrong, and people just conveniently "forget" to call me back. 

Which, actually, reminds me of the cable company. I had to call them three times on Tuesday just to get someone on the line, and the girl who finally answered sounded exactly like my niece, Sarah. Sarah just got her degree in communications, which is incredibly ironic because she never actually communicates. She never texts me back. I supervise a whole team of administrative support staff at my office, and I tell them all the time, "If you want to get something resolved, pick up the phone! Don't just send an email into the void." But nobody listens to the supervisor until something goes wrong with the filing system, and then suddenly I'm the most important person in the room... 

Anyway, what was I saying? Oh, right. The phone calls. So, everyone keeps telling me that all these things happening with my sister are just simple mistakes, just clerical errors. But I run an office. I know how things work. I know they’re deliberately keeping information from me and trying to push me out of the decisions.

symptom_reasoning.S019: The patient expresses a fixed, persecutory belief that people are deliberately keeping information from them and trying to push them out of decisions, despite evidence or reassurances that these are just clerical errors.
symptom_reasoning.S021: The patient exhibits tangentiality and derailment in their speech, drifting from the topic of their sister's appointments to the cable company, their niece, and their workplace before losing their train of thought and having to redirect themselves.

turns.doctor_question: How has your sleep been recently?
turns.patient_response: My sleep? Oh, it's fine, I suppose. I haven't really noticed anything different. I usually go to bed around 10:30, right after the local news. The anchors on channel 4 are just terrible lately, by the way. They replaced the main weather guy with this young kid who looks like he just graduated high school. It’s exactly like what HR is doing at my office, honestly—hiring these kids straight out of college who don't know a physical filing cabinet from a hole in the ground. I had to spend three hours yesterday explaining to a new hire how to use the label maker. Three hours! And she still jammed the tape. It's just a complete lack of basic common sense these days, you know? They just push buttons and hope for the best. I told my manager that if we keep cutting corners on training... wait, I'm sorry, what were we just talking about?

symptom_reasoning.S021: The patient exhibits tangential speech, drifting from the topic of sleep to the local news, then to workplace HR and a new hire, eventually forgetting the original question.
symptom_reasoning.S027: The patient explicitly states their sleep is fine and they have not noticed any changes.

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed any change in your energy levels recently compared to what's normal for you?
turns.patient_response:
My energy? No, not really. I have my usual amount of energy, I suppose. I mean, I have to, just to keep that office running. Honestly, I don't know where these younger girls get off complaining about being tired all the time. Just yesterday, Bethany—she's the one who jammed the label maker I was telling you about—was sighing heavily at her desk at two in the afternoon, saying she needed a fancy iced coffee to get through the day. An iced coffee! In my day, we just drank the drip coffee from the breakroom and got back to the filing. 

Speaking of the breakroom, they just switched our vendor for the snacks, and it’s a complete disaster. Half the vending machine is empty, and the other half is just those weird kale chips nobody eats. I had to email the vendor myself because, of course, nobody else took the initiative. It’s like pulling teeth trying to get anyone to take responsibility for the simplest things. If I didn't stay on top of them, the whole place would fall apart. Anyway... wait, what did you just ask me about? Was it about the coffee?

symptom_reasoning.S021: The patient exhibits tangential speech, drifting from the topic of energy to coworkers, coffee, and vending machines, ultimately forgetting the original question.
symptom_reasoning.S029: The patient explicitly denies experiencing fatigue or a lack of energy, stating they have their 'usual amount of energy.'
symptom_reasoning.S034: The patient denies any abnormal increase in energy, confirming they only have their 'usual amount of energy.'

turns.doctor_question: Have you ever heard voices or sounds that other people couldn't hear?
turns.patient_response:
Voices? No, no, nothing like that. I don't hear things that aren't there. I mean, the only thing I hear all day is the constant ringing of the phones because nobody else will pick them up. It's like they're deaf to it! Just this morning, the main line rang five times. Five times! And Bethany was sitting right there, staring at her phone, probably looking at those little videos everyone is so obsessed with now. I swear, the attention span of that generation is just completely shot. 

My niece Sarah is exactly the same way. I bought her a beautiful watch for her graduation—a nice, sensible Seiko, you know, something you can wear to an interview. And she looked at it like it was an alien artifact because it didn't have a screen that lit up. It's just baffling to me. People don't appreciate quality or craftsmanship anymore. It's all just disposable this and instant that. Which, frankly, is exactly what's happening with my sister's medical bills. They just run them through some automated system and don't even bother to have a real person look at them, and then they expect me to just accept that it's a "clerical error." I know better than that. I know exactly what they're doing. But... wait, sorry, what did you ask me? Did you ask about the phones?

symptom_reasoning.S019: The patient expresses a fixed, suspicious belief that the medical billing errors are intentional and part of a deliberate scheme ('I know exactly what they're doing').
symptom_reasoning.S020: The patient explicitly denies hearing voices or things that aren't there.
symptom_reasoning.S021: The patient's speech exhibits severe tangentiality and derailment, drifting from phones to a coworker, a niece, a watch, and medical bills before completely forgetting the original question.
